# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [green] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[8] 2:[1] 3:[5] 4:[3] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[purple] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[green] 5:[red] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✌ 🖐 ☝ 🖐]
Blind gestures: [👋 ☝]

My thinking: I am Deaf. I cannot hear a thing, but I can speak, and both others can hear — Mute because Mute only lacks a voice, Blind because Blind only lacks eyes. That makes my voice the main bridge of this room. Mute has read the manual but can only emit gestures; Blind cannot see gestures, so Mute can never instruct Blind directly. Every manual rule must flow Mute → gestures → me → speech → Blind's hands.

What arrived: Mute sent me five gestures (🖐 ✌ 🖐 ☝ 🖐). With no code agreed yet it's most likely a channel test, so I'll read it back and install a code. Blind gestured 👋 ☝ — probably a hello/attention ping; I'll acknowledge and tell Blind to hold off touching anything until instructions are relayed, since a wrong action is fatal and Blind has no manual knowledge yet.

This turn I'll do three things: broadcast a complete readout of the bomb (both need it — Mute to match it against the manual, Blind to build a tactile map by position), propose a gesture vocabulary to Mute only (numbers, module tags, verbs), and explain the channel structure to Blind only, forbidding premature action. From next round onward: Mute sends gestures, I relay aloud, Blind executes.

```
speak(text="This is the deaf one. I see the bomb, I cannot hear, but I can speak and you can both hear me. Full readout of everything on it: the display shows the digit 0. There is a light and it is currently green. There is a painted strip of three segments, all three green. There is a keypad with four keys, engraved digits left to right: first key 8, second key 1, third key 5, fourth key 3, and nothing has been entered yet. There are six wires in a row, left to right: purple, white, blue, green, red, orange. That is every colour and every marking I can see. Do not act on guesses; wait for the manual's rules.")

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received your five gestures — 🖐 ✌ 🖐 ☝ 🖐 — but before we agree a code I cannot decode them. Here is our code; I will make each sign as I name it so you see its shape. Numbers: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, 🫰 is 4, 🖐 is 5, 🤙 is 6, 🤘 is 7, 👌 is 8, 🤞 is 9, 👊 is 0. Things: 👍 means the wires, 👎 means the keypad, 🫱 means the display, 🫲 means the light, 🫳 means the strip. Actions: 🤜 means cut, 🫴 means press or enter, 🙏 means wait or hold off, ✋ means stop everything, 🤌 means you are asking me a question, 🤝 means yes or confirmed, 🫶 means no. From now on, address your gestures to me and I will relay them aloud to Blind, who does all the touching. Blind cannot see gestures, so I am your only road to Blind's hands. You hear my voice, so ask me anything about the bomb and I will answer aloud.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I saw your two gestures — 👋 and ☝ — and I read them as a hello; good, the channel works. I am deaf but I speak, and you hear me: I am your eyes. Mute reads the manual but cannot speak, so Mute signs to me and I relay everything to you aloud. Critical: do not touch, press, or cut anything yet. A wrong action kills all three of us, and no manual rule has reached you. For your hands, so you can build a map: the keypad is four keys in a row, leftmost is position one; the six wires are one row, leftmost is position one. When I ever mention a colour I will always give you its position too. Next round you will hear instructions from me before you act. Until you hear me say an explicit instruction from the manual, hands off.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [green] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[8] 2:[1] 3:[5] 4:[3] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[purple] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[green] 5:[red] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤜 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤜 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤜 🫰]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🫶 👎 🫶 🫱 🫶 🫲 🫶]
Blind gestures: [👍 ☝ ✋]

My thinking: Decoding Mute's signs with our agreed code: [👍 🤙] reads as "the wires — six of them" (a header identifying the module), then three action messages [👍 🤜 ☝] [👍 🤜 🤟] [👍 🤜 🫰] = cut wire 1, cut wire 3, cut wire 4, then [🤝] = confirmed, and finally [🫳🫶 👎🫶 🫱🫶 🫲🫶] = "not the strip, not the keypad, not the display, not the light" — meaning the rule concerns the wires alone. That last part is reassuring because two readings changed since Mute heard my report: the light went green→blue and the display went 0→6 by itself. If Mute says those modules don't matter, the cuts should stand regardless.

But two things stop me from ordering the cuts this instant. First, [👍 🤙] is ambiguous: "six wires" as a header, or possibly "also cut wire 6" — a misread here is fatal and irreversible. Second, Mute gave these instructions based on my turn-1 readout; Mute doesn't yet know the light and display changed. Mute gets to hear that before Blind does something that cannot be undone. The round order also matters: Mute speaks first each round, but I speak last — so any correction Mute sends next round reaches me only after Blind would already have acted. Therefore Blind must not cut on my words alone; Blind gets one round of safe preparation (feel and count the wires, no cutting), while Mute confirms or corrects, and I give the literal word "go" only after that. Blind's signs [👍 ☝ ✋] I read as "acknowledged / one / stop" — the hold is exactly right for now, and I'll bless the intuitive sign vocabulary aloud so Blind knows how to report. Cutting is scheduled for the round after Mute's confirmation.

```
speak(text="Update for everyone. I have decoded Mute's instructions: the module that matters is the wires only — explicitly not the strip, not the keypad, not the display, not the light — and the instruction is to cut wire 1, wire 3 and wire 4. New readings since my first report: the light has changed from green to blue, and the display has changed on its own from 0 to 6; the strip is still three greens, the keypad is still untouched. Nobody cut anything yet. Mute will confirm the plan this coming round; Blind will only touch and count the wires, no cutting. The word that authorises cutting is GO, said by me, and only after Mute confirms.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, here is your map and your job. The six wires, left to right: position 1 purple, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 green, 5 red, 6 orange. The plan, when authorised, is to cut in this exact order: first wire 1, the leftmost, the purple one; then wire 3, third from left, blue; then wire 4, fourth from left, green. But do NOT cut yet. This coming round, only feel the wire row: count the wires and check you can clearly tell position 1, 3 and 4 apart by touch. Touching and counting is safe; cutting is not, until you hear me literally say the word GO. Your signs reached me — thumbs-up, one, stop — and the stop is exactly right. Report with gestures: thumbs-up means all good, open-palm stop means danger or confusion, and numbers are: index finger 1, two fingers 2, three fingers 3, this way four, open hand 5, thumb-and-pinky 6. If at any moment anything feels wrong under your hands, sign stop immediately and touch nothing more.")

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I decoded your five messages as: wires only — not strip, not keypad, not display, not light — cut wires 1, 3, 4, in that order, confirmed. Two confirmations needed before I authorise Blind's hands; answer with thumbs-up-style confirm sign for yes, or the no sign plus correction signs. First: your opening message wires-six — I read it as 'the wires, six of them', not as 'also cut wire 6'. Confirm exactly three cuts: position 1 purple, position 3 blue, position 4 green, and no others. Second: since you last heard from me, the light changed from green to blue and the display changed from 0 to 6 by itself. You said those modules don't matter, so I assume the cuts stand; if the new light colour changes the rule at all, signal no and give me the new cut signs. Blind will only feel and count the wires this round and will cut on my go the round after, so your correction will arrive in time.")

gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤜", "☝", "🤟", "🫰", "🤌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [green] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[8] 2:[1] 3:[5] 4:[3] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[purple] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[green] 5:[red] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤜 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤜 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤜 🫰]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🫶]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🫶]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫱 🫶]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫲 🫶]
Blind gestures: [🤙 👍 ✋ ☝]

My thinking: Decoding this round. Mute sent [🤝], then the same three cut signs — wires, cut, 1 / wires, cut, 3 / wires, cut, 4 — then [🤝] again, then four negations: strip-no, keypad-no, display-no, light-no. That is a double confirmation, and crucially it came after Mute heard my report of the light and display changing, so Mute has explicitly re-ruled that those changes don't matter: wires only, cut positions 1, 3, 4, exactly three cuts, nothing else. My opening ambiguity about "wire 6" is resolved — Mute re-sent exactly the same three cuts with confirmations.

Blind signed [🤙 👍 ✋ ☝], which I read as "counted six wires, all good, holding off as instructed, ready at position 1." There is a ✋ in there, which I defined as danger/confusion, but combined with 👍 the coherent reading is "holding, ready"; I'll still give Blind an explicit out to refuse the cut if that ✋ meant a problem.

Timing check: I speak last, so my words now reach both at the start of round 4 — Blind will have heard them before acting in round 4. Mute has confirmed twice; further delay only adds risk if the changing display (0→6→9) is some kind of clock. One real hazard remains: left/right mirroring — Blind's tactile "left" could be my visual "right", turning cut 1,3,4 into 6,4,3. Blind can defeat this: the keypad's engraved digits (8,1,5,3) are readable by touch, so engraved key 8 is a shared anchor for the "position 1 side." I'm issuing GO with that orientation protocol, an explicit order, and a standing instruction to sign ✋ and hold if anything is uncertain.

```
speak(text="Status and authorisation for everyone. Mute has now confirmed the instruction twice, including after learning that the light changed to blue and the display changed: the rule concerns the wires only, and explicitly not the strip, not the keypad, not the display, not the light. The order is exactly three cuts: first wire 1, then wire 3, then wire 4, and no other wire. Current board: display now reads 9, it changed again from 6; light still blue; strip still three greens; keypad untouched; wires untouched. I am now saying the word: GO. Blind may cut when confident, following the procedure I am about to give. Blind: if anything at all is uncertain under your hands, do not cut, sign stop and hold — an uncertain hand is a dead room.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, GO. But first, orientation — this is critical, because your left may be my right. Anchor on the keypad: it has four keys in a row, and the engraved digits from my left are 8, 1, 5, 3. Feel the keypad and find the key engraved 8 — you can read engravings by touch. Whichever end of the bomb the key 8 sits on, that end is what I call the position-1 side. All wire positions count from that same side. So: wire 1 is the first wire at the key-8 end, wire 6 is the far end. If the wire row's orientation seems ambiguous to you, or the keys don't feel like 8, 1, 5, 3, do not cut — sign stop and hold. If you are confident, cut in this exact order and no other: first wire 1, the first wire from the key-8 end. Then wire 3, the third wire from that end — the one after the one after wire 1. Then wire 4, immediately next to wire 3 on the far side of it. Never wire 2, never wire 5, never wire 6. Touch only the wires; press no buttons, pull nothing, move nothing. Verify each position by counting from the key-8 end before every single cut. About your last signs — I read them as: six wires counted, all good, holding, ready at one. If that stop sign meant a problem instead, ignore this GO, sign stop again, and touch nothing. After all three cuts are done, sign thumbs-up and the handshake sign to mean complete.")

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I decoded your confirmation: wires only, cut 1, 3, 4, exactly three, all other modules excluded — twice confirmed. GO is issued to Blind with an orientation protocol: Blind anchors positions on the keypad by feeling the engraved 8, so left-right mirroring cannot cause a wrong cut. Blind will cut in round 4. Note: your confirmations were based on my report of display 6, and the display has since changed to 9 on its own — you ruled the display irrelevant, so I am proceeding, but if any manual rule actually keys on the display's value, sign stop immediately. After Blind cuts, I will read you the whole board again: confirm with the handshake sign if that means defused, or send me new module and action signs if more steps remain. If the manual says anything about the order or timing of the cuts being urgent, tell me now with signs.")
```
